<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-w46-nice-qantas-cut-jobs" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-w46/nice-qantas-cut-jobs/" data-aixpm-date="2026-11-10" data-aixpm-title="NICE and Qantas cut jobs months after saying they would not." markdown>

**NICE and Qantas cut jobs months after saying they would not.** NICE will cut about 500 roles (5% of roughly 10,000); its CEO cites R&D teams "leveraging AI tools to increase productivity materially" and the removal of "layers of management and span of control", after saying in July "We have no plans to reduce headcount." Qantas will cut around 850 back-office roles through an Accenture deal that moves most of the work to India first, with automation and AI to follow; its union says it was told earlier this year there was "no plan to offshore any jobs". In both cases the productivity claims are management's own. [CTech, 4 Nov 2026](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/ygubfbd9r) · [Information Age, 10 Nov 2026](https://ia.acs.org.au/article/2026/qantas-to-axe-850-jobs-in-ai-overhaul.html)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-10-gartner-13-percent-cios-value" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-10/gartner-13-percent-cios-value/" data-aixpm-date="2026-10-31" data-aixpm-title="Only 13% of CIOs report significant AI value, and stop rules separate the leaders." markdown>

**Only 13% of CIOs report significant AI value, and stop rules separate the leaders.** In Gartner's survey of 2,002 CIOs and technology executives, organisations with guidelines for when a pilot should not move to production are 2.3 times more likely to be "vanguards", yet only 31% have them. The figures are self-reported and show an association, not a cause. [Gartner, 19 Oct 2026](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-10-19-gartner-survey-finds-only-13-percent-of-cios-say-their-enterprise-has-realized-significant-or-transformational-value-from-ai)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-10-award-winning-workflow-cost" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-10/award-winning-workflow-cost/" data-aixpm-date="2026-10-31" data-aixpm-title="An award-winning AI workflow cost $12–14 per file against about 80 cents done manually." markdown>

**An award-winning AI workflow cost $12–14 per file against about 80 cents done manually.** An audit at an unnamed mid-sized enterprise found the 90% faster turnaround hid the bill: pilot costs sat in a central innovation fund, and roughly 40% of daily transactions fell into a human exception queue taking ten minutes each, twice the manual baseline. [CIO.com, 8 Oct 2026](https://www.cio.com/article/4232005/i-audited-an-award-winning-ai-project-the-case-study-left-out-the-cloud-bill.html)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-10-lawyers-ai-use-fees" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-10/lawyers-ai-use-fees/" data-aixpm-date="2026-10-31" data-aixpm-title="In a billable-hours profession, AI use rose to 55% but only 26% cut fees." markdown>

**In a billable-hours profession, AI use rose to 55% but only 26% cut fees.** A census of 2,221 lawyers by Victoria's legal regulator shows fee cuts are more common for business clients (34%) than for individuals (23%). The co-author says gains were lower than expected, possibly offset by verification, and 41% of lawyers now receive AI-generated client documents that need correcting. These are lawyers, not consultants. [The Guardian, 30 Oct 2026](https://www.theguardian.com/law/2026/oct/30/victorian-lawyers-ai-clients-fees)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-09-societe-generale-ai-gains-plan" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-09/societe-generale-ai-gains-plan/" data-aixpm-date="2026-09-30" data-aixpm-title="Société Générale writes €500–600M of AI gains into its 2026–2029 plan." markdown>

**Société Générale writes €500–600M of AI gains into its 2026–2029 plan.** The bank announced a partnership with Anthropic to deploy Claude at every level of the company, inside a €1.9bn gross cost-reduction target for 2029 that relies mainly on not replacing natural departures. These are investor-day targets, not results. Danske Bank made the same link that week: its headcount (19,472 FTEs) will keep falling as employees get personal AI agents by year-end. [Presse-citron, 22 Sep 2026](https://www.presse-citron.net/ia-et-restructuration-en-pleine-bourre-la-societe-generale-poursuit-son-incroyable-transformation/) · [Bloomberg via Briefs, 21 Sep 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/danske-expects-fewer-staff-as-ai-is-rolled-across-the-bank/)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-09-two-thirds-french-companies" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-09/two-thirds-french-companies/" data-aixpm-date="2026-09-30" data-aixpm-title="Two-thirds of French companies use generative AI; one-third see productivity gains." markdown>

**Two-thirds of French companies use generative AI; one-third see productivity gains.** In a Banque de France survey of about 7,000 firms, more than two-thirds of those with over 20 employees use generative AI tools, yet only a third report productivity gains. It blames experimental uses and imperfect integration into production processes. [AFP via Boursorama, 3 Sep 2026](https://www.boursorama.com/actualite-economique/actualites/ia-dans-les-entreprises-une-adoption-rapide-sans-effet-immediat-sur-la-productivite-c93eaecaf24c5eacb01ec56fcba787af)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-08-half-euro-area-employees" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-08/half-euro-area-employees/" data-aixpm-date="2026-08-31" data-aixpm-title="Half of euro-area employees now use AI, but the productivity gain is conditional." markdown>

**Half of euro-area employees now use AI, but the productivity gain is conditional.** An ECB note of 26 August puts usage at 52% of employees, up from 26% in 2024, with users reporting three hours saved per week. The bank warns that the gain only materialises if firms convert that time into output, service quality or innovation, a shift not all of them have started. [La Tribune, 26 Aug 2026](https://www.latribune.fr/article/tech/intelligence-artificielle/32821203213850/ia-au-bureau-trois-heures-gagnees-par-semaine-mais-le-miracle-productif-attendra)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-08-uk-government-kpmg-ey-contract" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-08/uk-government-kpmg-ey-contract/" data-aixpm-date="2026-08-31" data-aixpm-title="The UK government awarded KPMG and EY up to £456m to train civil servants, AI included." markdown>

**The UK government awarded KPMG and EY up to £456m to train civil servants, AI included.** According to Tussell data cited by the Financial Times, it is the largest single Big Four contract since records began in 2012, covering 2026 to 2028. The figure is a ceiling, not committed spend, and the Cabinet Office says it covers training rather than consultancy. [Consultancy.uk, 27 Aug 2026](https://www.consultancy.uk/news/45443/government-hands-kpmg-and-ey-huge-contract-for-ai-training-of-civil-servants)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-07-jpmorgan-ai-job-cuts" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-07/jpmorgan-ai-job-cuts/" data-aixpm-date="2026-07-31" data-aixpm-title="JPMorgan says AI has cut 30–40% of jobs in some units, and that margins will not grow as a result." markdown>

**JPMorgan says AI has cut 30–40% of jobs in some units, and that margins will not grow as a result.** On the second-quarter earnings call, Jamie Dimon said the bank had cut jobs by as much as 40% in some parts using AI, with most affected employees offered positions elsewhere in the firm. He told analysts "You don't uniquely benefit from AI": every bank deploys it, so no single institution pockets the savings. CFO Jeremy Barnum flagged token spending as a cost line the bank expects to accelerate. [The Next Web, 14 Jul 2026](https://thenextweb.com/news/jpmorgan-dimon-ai-jobs-cuts-margins-q2-earnings)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-07-gallup-organizational-adoption-jump" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-07/gallup-organizational-adoption-jump/" data-aixpm-date="2026-07-31" data-aixpm-title="Gallup measured a six-point quarterly jump in organisational AI adoption in the US." markdown>

**Gallup measured a six-point quarterly jump in organisational AI adoption in the US.** In the second quarter of 2026, 47% of US employees said their organisation had integrated AI tools, up from 41% the quarter before; 52% use AI in their role and 15% use it daily. The most common uses are not the ones rated most productive: 77% of those using AI for coding or automation report a positive effect, against 68% for writing and editing. [Gallup, 20 Jul 2026](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/712736/organizational-adoption-jumps-six-points.aspx)
